title: Generative UI V1 (2b of 4): the owner's settings and less chrome
requested_outcome: Owner-approved Generative UI V1 (docs/product-memory/GENERATIVE_UI_V1.md section 4), objective 2b of 4: user-facing settings and less chrome on the phone app. Today the Settings sheet (web/index.html dialog#settings, driven by web/app.js) mixes the owner's choices with engineering diagnostics, and the header shows connection and provider status permanently. Change it so that: (1) Settings reads as the owner's, in this order and in plain words: Voice (voice on or off, preview, microphone test); What CLIVE can do for you (the actions it may prepare, and that every change waits for the owner's tap), taken from what the app already loads; Who and what CLIVE can reach (each connected service - Shopify, Gmail, voice, transcription - as connected, or needs attention with the plain reason and what to do, such as voice paused because the credits are used up), taken from /health as it is; What CLIVE needs from you (only the open owner steps that /health or the app already reports); and Conversation (new conversation). A section with nothing true to show is left out, never filled with placeholder text. (2) Diagnostics and fixtures move behind the existing developer section, reached by a clearly labelled 'Developer view' switch at the bottom, off by default. (3) The header shows connection or service status only while something is wrong and it matters to what the owner is doing; when all is well it shows nothing. (4) Back, Previous and Next appear only while the owner is inside a list or a drill-down, never as a permanent strip, and keep working exactly as they do today when shown. (5) No owner-facing text names the Mac, a tablet, launchd or 'make up'. Use the existing design tokens in web/style.css; no new fonts or colours; generous spacing, fewer elements. No backend changes: use only data the app already fetches. Tests: node tests under tests/web (with the existing dom-shim) for the section order and omission of empty sections, the developer switch, the contextual header and the contextual navigation, run by a new test function in tests/test_web_js.py like the other node suites there; update any existing test in tests/test_web.py or tests/web that pins the old layout to state the new behaviour, and change nothing else in them. This objective continues from its own earlier candidate, the base commit 595d3a30 (branch clive/objective/generative-ui-v1-settings-chrome), where four rounds of independent review left two open findings (F-01, F-02) when the repair budget ran out; the review of your change will state them. Check the base against every acceptance criterion, close anything that falls short, and keep changes inside the allowed paths. tests/test_ui_semantics.py and tests/test_pwa.py also pin owner-facing text; if your change alters text they pin, update only those expectations. You cannot run commands: the loop runs the listed checks after you report and returns any failure output, and the independent review returns its findings, to your next attempt. Do not report an owner decision for GitHub acceptance: it runs automatically after your candidate is published.
acceptance_criteria: Settings shows only the owner's sections in the stated order, in plain words, with empty sections omitted
diagnostics and fixtures sit behind an off-by-default Developer view switch
the header shows status only while something is wrong and relevant, and Back, Previous and Next appear only inside a list or drill-down
no backend change and no owner-facing runtime-host wording
every listed check passes in the worker's workspace
